c.tagline: Bolivia's whitewashed constitutional capital, where colonial grandeur meets dinosaur tracks.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis charge a flat per-trip rate (a few bolivianos within the center); agree it before departing. Shared 'trufi' taxis run fixed routes. Ride apps have limited coverage.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 118 the ambulance service in Bolivia; 119 is the fire brigade. Response times can be slow outside the center.

hood_landmark.Centro Histórico: Plaza 25 de Mayo Sucre Bolivia cathedral

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the Mercado Central and around the bus terminal, and take a taxi rather than walking to the terminal or cemetery area late at night.

hood_desc: The whitewashed UNESCO colonial core around Plaza 25 de Mayo, home to the Cathedral, Casa de la Libertad, universities, museums, cafes and most hotels; the ideal walkable base for first-timers.

A tranquil hillside neighborhood just southeast of the center around the Recoleta convent and its arched mirador, with some of Sucre's prettiest colonial houses and sweeping city views; peaceful and scenic.
A quiet, leafy residential area north of the center favored by university students, longer-stay visitors and expats, with local markets and an easy walk into the old town.
A traditional, workaday barrio near the central market and El Tejar church just west of the historic core, with everyday shops, eateries and a local, unpolished feel; handy and central.
A calm residential district with parks and mid-range homes a short ride from the center; a relaxed, local base away from the tourist bustle.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water; avoid ice from unknown sources.

transit.hours: City micros generally run from around 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; after that taxis and shared trufis are the main option.
transit.note: Sucre has no metro or rail. Public transport is a network of micros (small city buses) and shared trufi taxis on fixed routes, backed by regular taxis. The compact historic center is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver on board (roughly Bs 2 per micro ride); there is no transit card. Carry small notes and coins.

bus: Intercity buses from the Terminal de Buses to Potosí, La Paz, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz

transit.m: Taxi to the city center (40-45 min)
Shared minibus / trufi from the airport toward the center (fills as it departs)

tip.r: Tipping is not deeply ingrained; 5-10% at tourist-oriented restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected, and rounding up is fine elsewhere.
